resources.string: Star an article to keep it here, even after it leaves its feed.
No articles yet. Pull down to refresh.
A calm, private reader for RSS, Atom and JSON feeds. Your feeds and what you read stay on this phone; Perch fetches them itself, with no account and no tracking.
A feed\'s or a site\'s address
Perch finds the feed a site links to.
No feed found at that address.
Couldn\'t find the article on its page.
A few well-known feeds per topic, picked by hand and listed in Perch\'s source. Add a whole pack into its own category, or just the feeds you want.
No feeds yet. Add one with + or pick some in Explore.
Its articles go too; starred ones stay.
Bars and buttons float over the content and bend what passes beneath them. Turn it off for solid surfaces.
That file isn\'t an OPML list.
Perch collects nothing. Feeds are fetched by this phone, without cookies.
Your library is on this phone. A sync chain keeps it in step with your other devices, end-to-end encrypted, with no account.

Your feeds, settings, notes and what you read, kept in step across your devices. Everything is encrypted on the device; the relay in between only passes on what it can\'t read. The code is the only key: whoever has it is in the chain.
This phone\'s library goes into the new chain. Then scan its code on your other devices.
Show the code on a device already in the chain (Settings → Sync chain), then scan it or type it here. The two libraries merge.
Point the camera at the chain\'s QR code.
That QR code isn\'t a Perch chain.
There\'s no chain with this code.
This server doesn\'t relay sync chains.
Couldn\'t reach the relay. Check your connection.
That code isn\'t complete or has a typo. It has 28 letters and digits.
This chain was deleted on another device.
Anyone with this code can read and change your library. Show it only to your own devices.
Each device says what it is. Removing one only hides it; to cut a device off, delete the chain and start a new one.
Your library stays on this phone; it just stops syncing. The other devices keep the chain.
Delete the chain for every device
The relay forgets it and every device stops syncing. Libraries stay on each device.
To share notes as public pages, sign in to a Perch Server you or a friend runs. Perch itself doesn\'t host accounts or pages, and your library stays on this phone either way.
On a Perch Server of your own
Only for sharing notes as public pages from your own server. Any note can also be shared as text.
Your notes stay private until you share one. Shared notes are public pages under this name.
Shown on shared notes. Better not your real name.
At least 8 characters. It never leaves this phone.
If you forget your password, this code is the only way back into your account. The server keeps only a scrambled copy. Keep it somewhere private.
This server isn\'t taking new accounts.
Proving you\'re not a bot… (a few seconds)
Couldn\'t reach the server. Check your connection.
That recovery code isn\'t complete. It has 20 letters and digits.
The new code replaces the old one. Enter your password to confirm.
Your other devices are signed out.
Your name and every shared page are removed from the server. Your notes stay on this phone. Enter your password to confirm.
No notes yet. Open an article and tap the note button to write one.
Sharing publishes a copy of this note at a random address on %1$s, under your Perch account\'s name.
Public pages need a Perch Server of your own (Settings → Perch account). You can always share a note as text.
This page was shared from another account. Sign in to it to stop sharing.

If you forget your password, this code is the only way back into your account. The server keeps only a scrambled copy, so nobody can tell it to you again. Store it somewhere private: a password manager, or printed and put away. Anyone with this code and your username can set a new password for your account.

1. Open Perch, choose Sign in, then \"Forgot your password?\".\n2. Enter your username, this code and a new password.\n3. Your other devices are signed out. You can make a new code in Settings, which replaces this one.
Asks for the PIN when Perch opens, and when you come back after a minute away. It keeps others out of the app, but doesn\'t encrypt the library on the phone.
This address only relays sync chains: there are no accounts on it. Use it under Settings → Sync chain.
Theme, colors, glass, background image and app icon
Light and dark keep their own colors. They sync with your chain, so your other devices match.
Text and borders adjust to stay readable on it.
Titles and article text; secondary text is a softer shade.
Unread dots, links, the tab bar and stars.
Filled buttons; their label colour is picked for contrast.
Shown behind every screen on this phone only. Panels turn translucent over it.
Only on this phone; your other devices keep theirs. Your launcher may take a moment to show it.
A notification when background refresh finds new articles. Turning it on turns background refresh on too.
Your unread count and the newest articles.
Keep the library on a server you or a friend runs
Perch works on its own. With a server you or a friend runs, your feeds and what you\'ve read follow you to the browser extension and the web. The feeds on this phone are added to the account.

Everything syncs through your Perch Server: feeds, read and starred articles, theme and colours, notes. Changes made offline are sent when you\'re back. Signing out deletes the offline copy and goes back to the library on this phone.
This server holds Perch accounts, not libraries. Sync with a chain, and sign in to it under Perch account to share notes.
That server isn\'t a Perch Server.
This server runs in a mode this version of Perch can\'t use yet.
This server has no accounts yet: the one you create now is its admin.
We\'ll email you a code to set a new password.
This server confirms your email address before you sign up. We\'ll send you a code.
We sent a 6-digit code to %1$s. It works for 10 minutes.
Get a code by email instead
The newest unread articles and every starred one stay on this phone, so they can be read without a connection. Read and star changes made offline are sent when you\'re back.
Offline · showing what\'s saved on this phone
Every browser and phone signed in to your account.
Used only to reset your password. The server keeps a hash of it, not the address.
An address is on the account
Someone signs up on this server with a code you give them; each works once.
%1$s is run by its operator, who is responsible for your data there.
%1$s is run by its operator, who is responsible for your data there. It hasn\'t published a privacy policy.
